auditlens.reply:
Yes

Recording the stop, seat, and timestamp in the card's committed rulings makes compliance auditable directly from git. Mandating foreground waiting prevents detached background watchers from silently editing without trace. A minor gap is that an unrecorded background process that fails to commit leaves no footprint in git without runtime telemetry, but requiring rulings to log the stop creates a verifiable prerequisite before any takeover commit appears in history.

CITE: records in the card's rulings the seat, the stop and the time.
